result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick B and give accurate, concrete reasons based on measure, size, leading and heading scale. Answer B is tighter and more decisive. It also catches a sharp detail: C's h1 has no line-height of its own, so it inherits the 2.1 body value. Answer A suggests six tweaks, and some go beyond small adjustments, such as changing the measure to 65ch, making the body size fluid and switching to an off-white background, which revise parts of B that already work. Answer B's tweaks are minimal, given as code and justified. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick B and give similar reasons tied to what the learner sees. Both also make the same mistake: 40rem is about 640px at the default 16px root size, not 720px, though the characters-per-line conclusion still holds. Answer A wins because it critiques each rejected option on its own, catches that C's h1 inherits the 2.1 line height, and keeps its tweaks small, while Answer B's six tweaks drift into scope creep (a ch-based width, a fluid body size, off-white backgrounds, image and list styles) and partly replace things in B that already work.
